value.title: Registration attempts: measure, then stop healthy re-registration
value.summary: Issue #145: after #134, registration ps still runs at about 0.64/s at rest, so healthy seats re-register every few seconds. Count registration attempts by path, mode and outcome, find which seats and triggers repeat, and stop repeats that change nothing.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Source: issue #145, and performance's attribution (governance roles/performance/outputs/2026-11-06-issue145-registration-attribution.md). seat.put isn't an attempt log: unchanged paneless resolutions return before writing it, and refusals write nothing. Leads: retired contexts with 30 s standby and HTTP 400 lease failures; receive and heartbeat re-attestation; per-call paneless shim registration (fits F44, the shim's per-call cost). Performance's advice: count first; don't blanket-cache positive proof by pid, start and pane. C27 as amended stays: at most one /bin/ps -p per host-named ancestor, never batched.

sections.name: goals
value: Issue #145: after #134, registration ps still runs at about 0.64/s at rest, so healthy seats re-register every few seconds. Count registration attempts by path, mode and outcome, find which seats and triggers repeat, and stop repeats that change nothing.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Anything another roadmap step owns; see roadmap 001.

value.claim: Count. The daemon records bounded counters of registration attempts by entry path (receive, heartbeat, shim call, lease retry, explicit register), mode (pane or paneless) and outcome (new, unchanged, refused with reason), exposed in pij-rs --json ping beside spawns. No new launch, no per-attempt event write.
Attribute. With the counters live on the fleet, a performance reading names the paths, and the seats where the daemon can tell, behind the residual ps rate, in a receipt attached to #145.

Stop no-op repeats. A repeat registration that would resolve to the same seat with nothing changed skips the ancestry ps. It's keyed on what proves nothing changed (for example, the seat's bound identity and the caller's own verified pid and start), not a blanket positive cache: a changed pid, start, pane or exec still triggers the full read. Retired or tombstoned contexts that keep retrying get refused cheaply (no ps), with the reason named once.

Client side. If a client (the Copilot extension, the OMP extension or the shim) re-registers on a timer while healthy, it stops, or only re-registers on a real change. The shim's per-call registration (F44) is either removed or made a no-op through AC3.

Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). The goal is cost: registration ps near 0/s at rest. Counters are in-process atomics; no new launch site, timer or poll. Live BEFORE and AFTER on the fleet (pij-rs --json ping twice, 60 s apart, with data.pid).

Docs and states. No workstream state changes (issue fix). The PR body says Delivers: none and Fixes #145. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Code to read first: crates/daemon/src/registration.rs (the paneless path and AncestryReads from #134), the receive and heartbeat re-attestation paths, the lease retry, crates/cli shim forwarding, .copilot/ and .omp/ extension registration calls. Measure on the live daemon only with niced pings. No migration expected.

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
